rationale: C01 plausibly supplied a material template for the child: both commemorate a one-hundredth anniversary over a designated centennial period, invoke a recent congressional joint resolution, recount the enduring national significance of the subject, and culminate in a presidential call for public observance through appropriate activities. C06 has a closely related centennial-observance structure, while C05 resembles the child's secondary appeal to governmental officials and organized civic groups, but neither matches the child as comprehensively as C01.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The years 1961 to 1965 will mark the one-hundredth anniversary of the American Civil War.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the one hundredth anniversary of Theodore Roosevelt's birth throughout the centennial year beginning October 27, 1957
shared_material.explanation: Both frame the subject as a one-hundredth anniversary observed throughout a defined centennial period.

shared_material.child_excerpt: By a joint resolution approved on September 7, 1957 ... the Congress ... requested the President to issue proclamations inviting the people of the United States to participate in those observances.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: in consonance with a request made by the Congress in its joint resolution approved by me on September 4, 1957
shared_material.explanation: Both use a congressional joint resolution as the immediate predicate for the proclamation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do hereby invite all of the people of our country to take a direct and active part in the Centennial of the Civil War.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: do hereby call upon the American people to observe the one hundredth anniversary ... by appropriate activities and ceremonies
shared_material.explanation: The central operative provision uses substantially parallel machinery: a nationwide presidential appeal for active public observance of a centennial.
